title: 8. Handling Missing Data
description: Detect missing values and apply mean, median, and mode imputation with scikit-learn.

blocks.content:
### Missing Value Imputation

Real-world data contains gaps (`NaN`).

![Missing Values Percentage per Column](/images/ml/chart_missing_data.png)

#### Imputation Strategies
- **Median Imputation**: Best for numeric columns with outliers.
- **Mean Imputation**: Good for symmetric numeric columns without heavy outliers.
- **Most Frequent (Mode)**: Best for missing categorical strings.

Missing data is a blank on a form. You can remove the row, fill a sensible value, or add a “was missing” clue, depending on why it is blank.

Never treat every blank as zero by habit. Zero is a real answer, while missing means you do not know the answer.

blocks.starterCode:
from statistics import median

ages = [22, 25, None, 29, 100]
known_ages = [age for age in ages if age is not None]
typical_age = median(known_ages)
filled_ages = [typical_age if age is None else age for age in ages]

print("Original values:", ages)
print("Median used for the blank:", typical_age)
print("Filled values:", filled_ages)

from statistics import median

ages = [22, 25, None, 29, 100]
known_ages = [age for age in ages if age is not None]
typical_age = median(known_ages)
